rationale: The first round studies reductions only because the gate placed the candidate rules inside the existing grammar.
A finite interface is one way a bound on consequential local information could show up.
Closure of the reduced chain is the grammar question attached to an exact interface.
A positive defect is a witness that the external signature is not predictively sufficient.
Neighbour sizes are how a claimed six-node distinction would have to be seen.
Composition is the same interface question asked of two designated structures at once.
The item budget decides which of these reductions can actually be calculated.
Propagation along a path index is a different size question from the number of nodes inside one structure.
Behaviour that the named questions do not classify is still part of the coherence map.
The unconstrained cells are the case in which the outside can ignore the inside.
The wedge cells are the case in which hidden current state changes the next outside law.
The same partitions are exact for unconstrained weights and inexact for both wedge rules.
A finer current-state profile can destroy an interface that was already exact.
Count and parity repair the one-hidden-pair cells by being that pair. They fail when several pairs are hidden.
For the soft wedge the exact interface-respecting description is the whole graph.
The absorbing argument explains the single deadlock and the single recurrent class. It does not explain the size of the closure gap.
Neighbour comparison shows no exact verdict that begins at six nodes.
The two rate values are the star and its complement under the balance identity.
The local boost changes two symmetry orbits. Greater path-index depths repeat the complement orbit.
Presence moves between the same two orbits, with an exact cancellation at N=4.
An exact unconstrained interface remains unconstrained_lazy.
A failed wedge reduction is not_markovian_on_interface. The round produced no new event shape.
One constructed composition preserves the qualitative split and changes the defect fractions.
The soft wedge exhibits no frozen cell whose exact interface is a fixed finite summary shorter than the whole graph.
The hard-wedge remainder is finite in each cell and changes with N, so it is not a stable local bound.
The qualitative classes are already present at N=3. Later sizes in the round repeat them on a larger carrier.
The frozen questions were answered by exact enumeration inside the item budget.
The destruction of an exact interface by a wedge-count refinement was not an opening question.
The exact N=4 presence cancellation, with a nonzero change in the law over graphs, was not an opening question.
Repeated defect fractions across neighbouring sizes are unexplained beyond the computed range.
The N=4 presence cancellation is exact for the frozen multiplier and lacks a general proof.
The interface failure is a fact about this grammar. It is not an ontological claim.
The two-triangle cut keeps unconstrained_lazy when the interface is exact.
The analytic leftovers of RRC-001 stay open. They are not promoted into the atlas queue.
The identity was produced by the coverage round. It is not an explanation of an RRC-001 cell.
The support deletion was produced by the coverage round. It is not a six-node claim and not an interface claim.
The table identity and the core's failure to separate these carriers were produced by the coverage round. They are not an order to add a degree observable, and not an explanation of an earlier cell.
The sample extends the atlas coverage of cardinality and factors. It does not appoint an explanation of an earlier cell, and it does not close ATLAS-Q08.
The bit tables still match across the chain and the branch. The incident templates do not. That contrast does not explain the earlier identity, and it does not close ATLAS-Q07.
The identity accounts for the atlas-004 incident-prohibit deadlock counts. It does not account for the multiply templates, the class counts, or the bit-rule identity.
atlas-003 varied list length on one 3-edge carrier. atlas-005 places one generator on three edge counts. The contrast is coverage. It does not explain the atlas-003 cells.

atlas-004 compared a Boolean incident template with a designated bit. atlas-006 compares eq 1 and ge 2 with a designated bit and does not rerun the Boolean present polarity. The contrast is which predicate was compiled. It does not explain the atlas-004 cells.

RRC-ATLAS-003 records that a shared weight table need not share degree sequences. Atlas-008 uses those baseline tables and compares strong lumpability of three label maps. The shared hashes do not decide the comparison. The contrast does not explain the earlier cells and does not close ATLAS-Q07 or ATLAS-Q10.

Atlas-005 used one modular generator and reported means beside hashes. Atlas-009 uses a different placement grid. Shared means in that grid do not identify the tables. The contrast does not explain the atlas-005 cells and does not close ATLAS-Q01.

Atlas-008 stored the position-indexed line graph. On the four-cycle empty list that cell has eight labels and is not exact. Atlas-010 stores the canonical and orbit labels of the same weight table, and those two are one exact partition of six labels. The same round stores one multiply. The qualification is the representation. It does not explain the atlas-008 cells and does not close ATLAS-Q10.

Atlas-010 stored one line-graph partition for the triangle multiply. Atlas-011's bare singleton intersection is that partition, so the stored defect is not a new cover law. The omission covers and the opposite-edge cover are different partitions. The qualification is which cover collapses to the earlier map. It does not explain the atlas-010 cells and does not close ATLAS-Q10.

Atlas-009 stored distinct factor-2 tables that share a stationary mean. Atlas-012 stores three factor-3 singles that share mean edges 13/8. Two of them are the path reversal of one table. The third matches that table only after a bit swap that is not a carrier automorphism. The shared mean is not evidence that the atlas-009 marginals have the same cause. The factor-2 path grid was not rerun. The contrast does not explain the atlas-009 cells and does not close ATLAS-Q01 or ATLAS-Q03.

Atlas-006 stored factor-3 eq-1 and ge-2 multiplies on five other carriers. Atlas-013 stores prohibits of those thresholds, and of eq 2, on one star. On that star eq 2 and ge 2 are the same table because the neighbourhood size is 2. The qualification is the effect and the neighbourhood bound. It does not explain the atlas-006 cells and does not close ATLAS-Q02 or ATLAS-Q09.

Atlas-008 stored an exact degree sequence on the baseline four-cycle and an inexact position-indexed line graph. Atlas-014 uses the same carrier. The empty list repeats the four-edge constant-1 table. The prohibit makes the degree sequence, the edge count, and the line graph inexact. The qualification is the law. It does not explain the atlas-008 baseline defects and does not close ATLAS-Q13.

Atlas-012 stored factor-3 multiplies on this three-edge chain and no block family. Atlas-015 uses the same carrier and the same empty-list table. Its four constrained lists are not those multiplies. The overlap maps are observations atlas-012 did not store. The qualification is the law and the observation. It does not explain the atlas-012 means and does not close ATLAS-Q03 or ATLAS-Q14.

Atlas-011 stored fixed-cover maps on a triangle and a four-cycle under one multiply. Atlas-015 stores potential and realised maps of one chain cover under an empty list, two prohibits, and two other multiplies. The qualification is the carrier, the effect, and the realised adjacency. It does not explain the atlas-011 defects and does not close ATLAS-Q10 or ATLAS-Q14.

Atlas-015 stored a prohibit of (1,2) when (0,1) is present and a multiply of (2,3) by 3 when (0,1) is present on the three-edge chain. Atlas-016 stores the same bit positions on edges (0,1), (1,2), and (3,4). The matrices match and the edge lists differ. The qualification is the carrier. It does not explain the atlas-015 overlap defects and does not close ATLAS-Q14 or ATLAS-Q02.

Atlas-012 stored a multiply of (0,1) when (2,3) is present. Atlas-016 stores the same bit positions, with unread edge (1,2) and condition edge (3,4). The matrices match and the edge lists differ. The component means differ because the vertex counts differ. The qualification is the carrier. It does not close ATLAS-Q02 or ATLAS-Q03.

The opening model does not add a dynamical primitive to the single-toggle grammar. Atlas-017 stores six laws under method event-kernel-0.1.0 and leaves the engine string rrc-0.4.0. The all-ones two-bit catalogue and the identified toggle stay inside one-step single-toggle support. The joint cell and the coupled cell put positive probability on a Hamming-distance-2 target. That is a support difference under the named clock, not a new primitive of rrc-0.4.0 and not a new coordinate. The qualification does not close ATLAS-Q06.

Atlas-017 matched a one-bit identified toggle with two joint-copy transitions on an agreement image. Atlas-018 checks the full three-bit to four-bit inclusion under a strict method, distinguishes invariant coupled copies from free-copy leakage, and leaves the older records and method unchanged. The larger image check qualifies the earlier local correspondence without closing ATLAS-Q10 or claiming a new primitive.

The proof and independent 256-entry recoding check use the verified stored coupled law. They are post-execution analysis, not extra frozen scientific items, and do not change the originally declared image or event kinds.

The named four-bit joint step is outside same-coordinate one-step single-toggle support. A declared XOR recoding nevertheless gives an ordinary three-toggle kernel with a frozen disagreement bit. This qualifies the encoding boundary; it does not claim every event law compiles or that the new basis preserves the original relational meaning.
